Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments — downloading now. A few clarifying questions before we set the deep-dive: 

1) Backups: does Redwood replicate backups to a secondary region by default? If so, where are the backups stored and encrypted (same region as primary or central)?
2) Cross-region failover: is failover automatic or opt-in? If automatic, are we able to exclude certain customer data from being replicated?
3) KMS / keys: can we use our own customer-managed keys (KMS) in our cloud account and ensure keys never leave the region?
4) Logs / telemetry: where are request/response logs and model telemetry stored by default and what retention controls exist (we have a 7-year retention baseline for certain records)?
5) EU pinning: if we later expand to EU workloads, can we pin both models and logging to EU-only and ensure no tokens leave EU for inference?

Would like short answers on the above so I can share with our Infosec lead — I can then confirm folks for the technical session.

Samir —

Appreciate the clear list — answers below (high level) and I've attached the same diagram + SOC2 summary for your Infosec team. Aditya (copied) can add infra details on the call.

1) Backups: By default Redwood stores backups in the same region as the primary instance. Backups are encrypted at rest. Cross-region backup replication is not enabled by default — it is an opt-in setting per customer. When enabled, replication destinations are configurable and require customer approval. (See region-pinning-diagram.png, section "Backup & DR")

2) Cross-region failover: Failover is opt-in. We support two models: 
   - Manual/controlled failover: customer initiates DR, replicas are brought up in the target region.
   - Automated failover (advanced): available for customers who require <n> RTO/RPO; this requires explicit enablement and cross-region replication consent.
   We can exclude specific datasets from replication by policy (e.g., PII-only sets) — we'd align on rules during onboarding.

3) KMS / keys: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) integrated with your cloud KMS. Keys can be provisioned and scoped to a region; the Redwood control plane will not store plaintext keys. We also support HSM/KMS integrations for Private deployments.

4) Logs / telemetry: Request/response logs and model telemetry are stored in the same region by default. Retention is configurable at the workspace level — defaults are 90 days but can be extended or set to meet your 7-year requirement. We can also provide an export pipeline to your S3/GCS in-region for long-term archival and auditing.

5) EU pinning: Yes — you can pin inference and logging to EU-only for EU workloads. Our smart routing and model variants ensure inference stays within the chosen region. Cross-region inference (i.e., model execution in non-EU) will not occur for pinned workloads unless failover is triggered and explicitly approved.

Next steps I propose: 
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) to review KMS configuration, retention policies, and the failover workflow. Aditya can walk the infra specifics and Marissa will share the compliance artifacts.
- Pre-read: SOC2 summary + region-pinning diagram + the short FAQ I attached.

Proposed times: Thu Apr 29 9:00am PT, Thu Apr 29 11:00am PT, or Fri Apr 30 10:00am PT. Which works for your team?

If helpful, we can also scope a short pilot with region-pinning and export-to-S3 for audit retention.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
